results.title: AI4CE Update: A Comparative Study of AI-based CubeSat Design Generation Against Real-World Systems
results.abstract: The current progress of the AI4CE system is presented, an open-source tool developed for the automated generation of conceptual space system designs, with an initial focus on CubeSat configurations. Designed to benchmark AI-based methods against conventional approaches, the tool utilizes Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to rapidly synthesize design solutions within a Concurrent Engineering (CE) framework. To facilitate integration with established Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) environments, the generated designs are directly exported into an ECSS 10-25 compliant COMET model and SysMLv2 format. The primary objective of the work is to investigate the feasibility and potential benefits of using DRL to generate complete satellite designs and to determine whether an AI-driven process can offer advantages over traditional design methodologies. Several challenges inherent to CubeSat system design are addressed, including multidimensional optimization, a vast combinatorial design space, varying subsystem complexities, and the formulation of multiple constraints. A composite evaluation function has been employed to quantitatively assess each generated design based on the degree of requirement fulfillment, along with secondary metrics such as mass, cost, and power consumption. It is hypothesized that a design which satisfies a higher number of mission-specific requirements—and excels in additional performance parameters—demonstrates the high potential impact of AI-based system generation in accelerating CE studies. A case study based on the OPS-Sat mission is detailed, wherein a requirements report was used to drive the system generation process. A pre-trained Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent was tasked with generating a CubeSat design from a comprehensive database of available components. The resulting design was then systematically compared with an existing, real-world configuration by evaluating the fulfillment of requirements and additional performance criteria. Preliminary results indicate that design iteration times have been reduced from hours or days to mere minutes, thereby enabling rapid exploration and refinement of diverse design alternatives. Planned future developments include the expansion of the component database, the refinement of DRL algorithms, and the integration of alternative static optimizers to further enhance the system’s performance. In addition, the versatility of the approach is expected to extend its applicability beyond CubeSats to other modular systems such as drones, rovers, tiny houses, space stations, and ground segments. The implementation of AI-driven system generation, as demonstrated by AI4CE, is anticipated to contribute significantly to the democratization of space system design and to accelerate the overall system engineering process by enabling faster, more efficient, and innovative design solutions. For more information about AI4CE: https://ai4ce.space
